prayerExcerpt.en-US: It is not feeling, but self-love, which corrupts friendship.
prayerExcerpt.pt-BR: Não é o sentimento, mas o amor-próprio, que corrompe a amizade.

meta.face: An Englishman of about fifty-five, clean-shaven, with a fair, lightly flushed complexion and a LONG face that ends in a SOFT, ROUNDED chin — a smooth forehead, a short nose with a gently UPTURNED tip, very LARGE, soft, wide-set grey eyes under HIGH, ARCHED light-brown brows that give an open, tender look, faint hollows beneath the cheekbones, a WIDE, generous mouth in a slight, warm smile; a ring of short auburn hair turning grey around the monastic tonsure; the gaze kind and direct, toward us.
meta.basis: No portrait from life survives; the twelfth-century initial of a Speculum caritatis manuscript (Wikipedia lead image) shows a young, hooded, clean-shaven Cistercian, and Cistercian choir monks were shaven and tonsured, so the card is too. His biographers' picture of a man of great tenderness, 'a singularly attractive figure' (Knowles, quoted on Wikipedia), and his book on friendship give the open, smiling face; the structure is our choice, kept apart from `william_bourges` (wide, flat, bearded) and `bernard_clairvaux`.
